questions.question: When would you use Active Record vs raw SQL in Rails?
questions.title: Active Record vs Raw SQL
questions.direct_answer: Active Record (Rails ORM) maps tables to Ruby classes: User.find(1), User.where(active: true) generate SQL for you — readable, safe (parameterized), and schema-aware. Use it for normal CRUD and simple queries. Use raw SQL (find_by_sql, exec_query, connection.execute) when you need something AR can't express efficiently: complex joins/aggregations, window functions, a query that AR turns into N+1, or bulk operations. Even then, bind parameters (find_by_sql(['... WHERE id = ?', id]); connection.query_to_select) to avoid injection. Trade-off: AR is faster to write and easier to maintain but slower for complex queries; raw SQL is fast and expressive but loses AR's safety/conveniences and must be hand-bound. Rule: reach for AR first; drop to raw SQL only when AR is awkward or too slow, and always parameterize.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know AR is the default (readable/safe) and raw SQL is for complex/perf-critical queries — but must be parameterized.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Using raw SQL with string interpolation (injection) — always bind; or avoiding raw SQL even when N+1 hits.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: AR for normal CRUD/simple queries (readable, safe). Raw SQL for complex joins/aggregates/bulk where AR is awkward/slow — but parameterize.

Use raw SQL (find by sql, exec query, connection execute) when you need something AR can't express efficiently: complex joins or aggregates, window functions, a query that AR turns into N+1, or bulk operations. sections.title: AR vs Raw SQL
sections.content:
AR for normal CRUD (readable, safe). Raw SQL for complex/bulk where AR is awkward/slow — but parameterize.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  N[normal CRUD] --> AR[Active Record]
  AR --> S[safe, readable]
  C[complex joins / aggregates] --> R[raw SQL]
  B[bulk / perf-critical] --> R
  R --> P[MUST bind params]
```

sections.title: Active Record vs raw SQL
sections.content:
```ruby
# Active Record (default): maps tables to Ruby classes, generates safe SQL
User.find(1)                          # SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = 1
User.where(active: true)              # ... WHERE active = TRUE (parameterized)
User.joins(:posts).where(posts: {published: true})
User.order(created_at: :desc).limit(10)
User.count                            # SELECT COUNT(*)
# Readable, safe (parameterized), schema-aware. Use for normal CRUD.

# Raw SQL: when AR is awkward or too slow.
# 1) Complex joins / aggregates AR can't express well:
User.find_by_sql(['SELECT users.*, COUNT(p.id) AS pc
                    FROM users LEFT JOIN posts p ON p.user_id = users.id
                    GROUP BY users.id HAVING COUNT(p.id) > ?', 10])

# 2) Window functions / DB-specific features:
User.connection.execute("SELECT id, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC) FROM users")

# 3) Bulk updates (faster than updating records one-by-one):
User.update_all('last_seen = NOW()')        # AR bulk (still AR)
User.connection.update("UPDATE users SET status = 1 WHERE id IN (1,2,3)")

# 4) Reporting queries (read a few columns, many rows):
result = User.connection.exec_query("SELECT DATE(created_at) d, COUNT(*) c FROM signups GROUP BY d")
result.to_a  # [{"d"=>..., "c"=>...}, ...]

# ALWAYS BIND PARAMETERS with raw SQL (avoid injection):
#   BAD:  "... WHERE name = '#{name}'"          # injection
#   GOOD: ['... WHERE name = ?', name]            # bound
# Trade-off: AR = faster to write, safe, easy; raw = fast, expressive, must hand-bind.
# Rule: AR first; raw SQL only when AR is awkward/slow; always parameterize.
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Using raw SQL with string interpolation (injection) — always bind parameters.
Avoiding raw SQL even when AR causes N+1 or is too slow (drop down, but parameterize).
Selecting huge columns when you need a few (use pluck / select for lean rows).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: Active Record maps tables to Ruby classes; generates safe, parameterized SQL.
Use AR for normal CRUD and simple queries (readable, safe, schema-aware).
Use raw SQL for complex joins/aggregates, window functions, bulk ops, or N+1 cases.
With raw SQL, ALWAYS bind parameters (['... WHERE id = ?', id]) to avoid injection.
AR is faster to write; raw SQL is faster to run for complex queries — reach for AR first.

sections.title: Spoken Answer
sections.content: Active Record (Rails ORM) maps tables to Ruby classes: User find 1, User where active true generate SQL for you — readable, safe (parameterized), and schema-aware. Use it for normal CRUD and simple queries. Use raw SQL (find by sql, exec query, connection execute) when you need something AR can't express efficiently: complex joins or aggregates, window functions, a query that AR turns into N+1, or bulk operations. Even then, bind parameters (find by sql with a WHERE id question mark id; or exec query with binds) to avoid injection. Trade-off: AR is faster to write and easier to maintain but slower for complex queries; raw SQL is fast and expressive but loses AR's safety and conveniences and must be hand-bound. Rule: reach for AR first; drop to raw SQL only when AR is awkward or too slow, and always parameterize. A common mistake is using raw SQL with string interpolation, an injection risk, when you should always bind parameters.
